subject.title: refactor(channels): centralize inbound orchestration and remove internal compat

question: Should this all-channel ownership refactor land as one stack after representative upgrade and live-channel proof, or be narrowed before merge?
rationale: The patch deliberately moves a lifecycle owner boundary and changes public runtime/SDK surfaces across nearly every bundled channel; automated tests alone cannot decide whether the single-stack blast radius and rollout evidence are acceptable.

options.title: Prove and land the stack
options.body: Resolve the failed contracts, validate the packaged Plugin SDK and doctor migration, then run representative DM, group, topic/thread, retry, and delivery scenarios before landing the coherent refactor.

options.title: Narrow before landing
options.body: Split compatibility/config or adjacent subsystem cleanup from the inbound-kernel migration if the broad proof cannot isolate failures or establish upgrade safety.

recommendation.title: Prove and land the stack
recommendation.body: Resolve the failed contracts, validate the packaged Plugin SDK and doctor migration, then run representative DM, group, topic/thread, retry, and delivery scenarios before landing the coherent refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the linked design issue and authored the complete boundary-changing stack, so they are best positioned to decide whether the single-PR landing strategy is intentional.
